sentence: This project uses machine learning on medical record datasets to find patients with Alzheimer's disease and study how it affects stroke treatment and outcomes.
This project studies how Plasmodium vivax invades red blood cells of Duffy negative people, using genomic methods.
This project tests whether measuring the decay times of fluorescent dyes in cancerous tissue can show tumor margins during head and neck cancer surgery.
This project builds computer tools that use machine learning on genomics and drug screening data to help model diseases and find treatments.
This project sets up a shared facility with brain imaging equipment, including magnetoencephalography and MRI scanners, for studying the living human brain.
This project uses CRISPR tools to edit the genome, epigenome and transcriptome of primary human T cells to make safer and more effective cancer therapies.
This project builds and maintains a resource of tools for analyzing bacterial and viral pathogens and preparing for pandemics.
This project studies how skin and immune cells interact to cause lasting inflammation and sensitivity to ultraviolet light in lupus skin disease.
This project tests whether a genetically-informed intervention helps physicians order, and patients complete, lung cancer screening and tobacco treatment in primary care.
This project studies what ecological factors drive rabies spillover from wildlife to humans and livestock, and why some geographic areas are infected.
This project develops technology to assemble fully complete human genome sequences and find genetic variation in humans and model organisms.
This project studies how differences between tumor cells and their spread contribute to treatment resistance in metastatic bladder cancer, using patient samples and genomic sequencing.
This project studies how breast cancers evade the immune system and what factors shape the immune cells found inside tumors.
This project studies how a ketone body reprograms microglial metabolism to reduce tau pathology and neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds a catalog of somatic mosaicism in schizophrenia and autism and tests which variants may cause disease, using genomic and stem cell methods.
This project studies how HIV uses an endocytic pathway in macrophages to move captured viruses inside the cell and form a structure that stores virus.
This project builds easy-to-use software that works with multiple data types to help users understand how DNA methylation patterns cause cancer.
This project offers lab tests that measure hormones and metabolites to support studies of diabetes and insulin resistance in human subjects and animal models.
This project searches genomes for links to dental caries and periodontitis, builds polygenic risk scores, and looks for gene-by-environment interactions.
This project studies neurons made from stem cells of people with schizophrenia to find what goes wrong and how it links to symptoms.
